paragraphs: Your fulton County
Fulton County has announced two suicide prevention training sessions for September 2026 in recognition of National Suicide Prevention Month.

The Fulton County Department of Community Development, in partnership with 21st Century Leaders, Georgia’s premier youth leadership nonprofit organization, is once again engaging, empowering, and inspiring high school students from across Fulton County to become the next generation of leaders.

Fulton County is once again preparing to hit the court! In recognition of National Recovery Month, the Fulton County Accountability Courts and the Department of Behavioral Health & Developmental Disabilities (BHDD) are hosting the "Rebound for Recovery" 3-on-3 Basketball Tournament
Election season kicks off in Fulton County in less than 60 days. To prepare voters, the Department of Registration and Elections is preparing for 2 major celebrations.

The Fulton County Board of Commissioners will hold the scheduled Second September Meeting at Fulton County Government Center’s Assembly Hall on Wednesday, September 16, 2026 at 10 a.m. in the Fulton County Government Center Assembly Hall, 141 Pryor Street, NW Atlanta, GA 30303.

The Department of Arts & Culture presents, “A Dope Piece of Fruit, Closed Mouths Get Fed Strange Fruit,” a solo exhibition featuring the work of contemporary artist Brian Hebert from Friday, September 11 – Saturday, October 17, 2026 at the Emma Darnell Aviation Museum and Conference Center, 3900 Aviation Circle, NW Atlanta, GA 30336 and Fulton County Government Center, 141 Pryor Street, SW Atlanta, GA 30303.

In recognition of National Preparedness Month, the Atlanta-Fulton County Emergency Management Agency (AFCEMA), in partnership with the Georgia Emergency Management and Homeland Security Agency (GEMA/HS) and the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), is encouraging residents to prepare for emergencies and disasters before they occur.

The Fulton County Board of Registration & Elections will convene for its regularly scheduled September meeting on Thursday, September 10, 2026, at 11 a.m. at the Fulton County Government Center, 141 Pryor Street, SW, Atlanta, GA 30303.

The Fulton County Continuum of Care Board will meet virtually on Thursday, September 17, 2026, from 8 a.m. to 10 a.m. to receive updates and discuss business items. Citizens who wish to participate in the CoC Board Meeting must register in advance.

Love is back on the calendar. Fulton County’s Probate Court is officially relaunching its popular “Forever Fridays” wedding ceremonies beginning Friday, September 4, 2026, giving couples a fun, memorable and completely free way to say, “I do.”
This September, Fulton County recognizes National Recovery Month to build deeper community understanding around mental health and substance use disorders.

Georgia counties are charged with responsibility for health and human services, and Fulton County takes that responsibility seriously. In 2026, Fulton County will invest more than $100 million in health & human service programs.

Fulton County Vice Chair Khadijah Abdur-Rahman is inviting community members to join her for the 3rd Annual Mighty 6 'Cleared for Takeoff" Domestic Violence Awareness 5K. The race kicks off at 9 a.m. on Saturday, October 10, 2026, at the Fulton County Executive Airport at 3977 Aviation Cir NW, Atlanta, GA 30336.
The Fulton Fresh Mobile Market is once again gearing up to travel across the county this autumn to provide fresh, nutritious produce to local residents.
The Fulton County Tax Commissioner will mail all 2026 property tax bills on Saturday, August 15. Tax bills can also be viewed online at www.fultoncountytaxes.org.

paragraphs: Enter your address to find out which district you live in (City, State & Zip Code are not required). If you live in an apartment complex, please use the main address to the leasing office.

Fulton County is the most populous County in Georgia. According to the U.S. Census Bureau's 2025 estimates, the population of Fulton County is 1,098,791. Each commission district is home to approximately 183,131 residents.
fulton county

Fulton County is governed by a seven-member Board of Commissioners who are elected to four-year terms. Six of the members are district commissioners, and the Chairman is At-Large, representing all of Fulton County. The Board of Commissioners meets on the first and third Wednesday of each month at 10 a.m. Meetings are live streamed on FGTV.
Bridget Thorne is the Commissioner for District 1 which encompasses Johns Creek, and parts of Roswell, Alpharetta, and Sandy Springs.
Bob Ellis is the Commissioner for District 2 which encompasses Milton, Mountain Park and large parts of Alpharetta, Roswell and Sandy Springs.
Dana Barrett is the Fulton County Commissioner representing District 3 which includes all of Buckhead, and parts of both Sandy Springs and Midtown.
Vice Chair Khadijah Abdur-Rahman is the Fulton County Commissioner for District 6, popularly known as “The Mighty6” commission district.
